RQ1._question: Do LLM vulnerable-clone detectors rely on memorized surface form (verbatim vs certified slice-preserving variant; seen vs unseen CVEs)?
llm_detectors: Open-weight instruct LLM detector (e.g., StarCoder2/CodeLlama, elatoubi2025assessing-style prompting)
RAG-based LLM vulnerability detector (antal2026evaluating / kaniewski2026revisiting style)
Ungrounded LLM patching (same LLM, no slice/CVE grounding) — primary RQ3 baseline

membership_probe._note: lexical proxy, not an LLM likelihood probe; seen items form the reference set, so AUC ~1 is trivial

statistical_tests.test_used: McNemar (exact binomial for few discordant pairs), LLM detectors' pooled per-item correctness, verbatim vs certified variant; effect = accuracy gap; 95% paired bootstrap CI over items

RQ2._question: Does slice-preserving transformation of contaminated CVE clones yield a benchmark on which detection accuracy reflects semantic generalization rather than training-set recall?

statistical_tests.test_used: DiD paired bootstrap 95% CI + Wilcoxon signed-rank over per-CVE deltas (Holm-Bonferroni); Wilson CIs for yield/invariance; McNemar recall-collapse control

RQ2._annotator_agreement_note: Cohen's kappa computed between the certification signal and an independent automated structure-preservation (fingerprint/def-use) signal on accepted variants (CPU, no human labels). Full human kappa labelling is deferred to the researcher-run arm.

_decision.note: VPR comparison flagged INVALID (not evidence) unless the oracle precondition holds: official-accept>=0.90 and false-accept<=0.10.

RQ3._question: Can an agent that grounds LLM detect-verify-patch decisions in SRC VUL slice signatures and CVE patch diffs produce validated patches more reliably than ungrounded LLM patching?

statistical_tests.test_used: McNemar on VPR (slice-grounded-full vs best ungrounded), Holm-Bonferroni; Wilson CIs for VPR/oracle rates; severance-vs-oracle MCC/kappa; Wilcoxon on iterations

RQ3._data_binding_note: RQ3 bound to CVE vulnerable/fixed patch pairs (Big-Vul/CVEfixes or VulSlicer+VUDDY foundation corpus). GLUE was NOT used — it is a text-classification benchmark, not CVE patch data.
